guided_chapters.title: Meet titin in the sarcomere
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Titin is one continuous giant protein running from the Z-disc toward the sarcomere center. Here it is shown in red beside actin and myosin so its full half-sarcomere route stays visible.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: The continuous axial topology and domain order are constrained, while the smooth three-dimensional backbone path remains a schematic presentation of unresolved transverse placement.
not_claimed: known transverse azimuth along the entire chain

guided_chapters.title: Different regions extend differently
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Stretch does not scale every part of titin equally. Folded Ig chains mainly straighten, while disordered spring regions such as PEVK take a larger share of extension in the force-balanced model.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Regional nanometer partitions are modeled by a common-force series-chain solver using sourced force-extension laws; the interpolation is explanatory geometry, not a measured time trajectory.

guided_chapters.title: Elastic spring, anchored scaffold
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Titin changes role along its length. Its I-band regions form the extensible spring, while the long A-band segment remains integrated with the thick filament and leads toward the M-line.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Sequence architecture and axial organization support a heterogeneous molecule with elastic I-band elements in series with an A-band scaffold; exact unresolved linker conformations are not supplied.
not_claimed: one elastic constant for the whole molecule
